Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Toshimitsu Motegi, Foreign Minister of Japan, held a telephone conversation at noon on Tuesday, discussing and exchanging views on bilateral issues as well as the latest regional and international developments. The Iranian foreign minister attributed responsibility for the current tensions in the region to the United States’ regrettable violation of its commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum, stressing that the solution is simple. He said the US side’s return to and compliance with its commitments and its signature under the Islamabad Memorandum would pave the way for a return to normal conditions. Araghchi also outlined the latest status of Iran-Oman talks on the Strait of Hormuz, reporting significant progress in the two countries’ discussions on establishing a temporary transit route through the strait. He stressed the need to continue consultations between the two countries to reach an agreement on mechanisms for the future management of the Strait of Hormuz. Japan’s foreign minister, for his part, expressed concern over the escalation of tensions in the region and stressed the need for continued consultations and diplomatic coordination among regional countries and other stakeholders, with the aim of ensuring security in the region and free and safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian and Japanese foreign ministers also agreed to follow up on a number of bilateral and consular issues.

item.title: Iran FM holds phone call with new OIC Secretary-General
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi held a phone conversation on Monday with Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed, the newly appointed Secretary-General of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC). The Foreign Minister congratulated Ould Cheikh Ahmed on his election as OIC Secretary-General and wished him success in his new position. Araghchi expressed hope that, by drawing on the organization’s capacities, the new Secretary-General would play a role in strengthening the unity and coordination of Islamic countries in addressing developments and challenges facing the Muslim world. During the call, Araghchi briefed the OIC Secretary-General on the latest regional developments following the US and Israeli regime’s aggression against Iran, stressing the need for responsible action by Islamic countries in response to violations of Iran’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the need to counter the use of force and aggression. The Foreign Minister also referred to the critical circumstances and challenges facing the Muslim world, particularly the continuation of the Israeli regime’s aggression and crimes in Palestine and Lebanon. He stressed the need for firm support for the rights of the Palestinian and Lebanese peoples and for Islamic countries to adopt united and effective positions on these developments. Araghchi also invited the new OIC Secretary-General to visit Tehran and expressed hope that the visit would take place at the earliest appropriate opportunity.

item.title: Iran condemns US illegal attacks on Iranian vessels
item.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran strongly condemns the US act of aggression in attacking Iranian commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman on Saturday, September 5. These illegal and aggressive acts, carried out as a continuation of the US military aggression against Iran and as part of that regime’s maritime blockade and economic war against our homeland, constitute a clear violation of Paragraph 4 of Article 2 of the United Nations Charter, a war crime, and an overt threat to international peace and the security of commercial shipping. Emphasizing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to firmly defend its sovereignty and national interests against state terrorism and US acts of aggression—including the continuation of the maritime blockade and economic war and attacks on commercial vessels—the Ministry of Foreign Affairs stresses that responsibility for the consequences arising from the continuation of US aggressive and interventionist actions in the region will rest with the US regime and its accomplices and partners.

item.title: Iran condemns Niamey attacks reaffirms support for Nigers sovereignty stability
item.description: Esmail Baghaei, the Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, condemned the violent incidents and attacks in Niamey, the capital of Niger, which resulted in the death and injury of a number of military personnel and civilians. Expressing sympathy with the families of the victims and declaring solidarity with the people and government of Niger, the Foreign Ministry spokesperson emphasized the Islamic Republic of Iran's support for the Nigerien government's efforts to protect the country's independence and national sovereignty, maintain security and stability, and advance its national development programs.

item.title: New Iranian Consul General in Basra meets FM Araghchi
item.description: Mostafa Tarfī, the newly appointed Consul General of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Basra, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi prior to his departure for his new post and presented a report on his area of responsibility and the existing capacities, along with his proposed plan. During the meeting, the Foreign Minister, referring to the very good relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Iraq as two neighboring and Muslim countries, stressed the need to further deepen bilateral relations in the political, economic, social and cultural spheres and to make optimal use of Iraq’s capacities, given the many commonalities between the two countries.

item.title: New Iranian Consul General in Kazan meets FM Araghchi
item.description: Mohammad Basraei, the newly appointed Consul General of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Kazan, Russia, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi prior to his departure for his new post and presented his proposed plan for advancing affairs in his new position. The Foreign Minister wished the new Iranian Consul General in Kazan success and, referring to the importance of relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Russia, stressed the need to work toward strengthening relations with the Republic of Tatarstan and other republics and regions in Russia’s Volga area in all fields of mutual interest, particularly in the economic, tourism, academic and consular sectors. Prior to his appointment as Iran’s Consul General in Kazan, Basraei served as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs’ treasurer and Director General for Financial Affairs.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://en.mfa.gov.ir/portal/newsview/793705

Bassem Naim, a member of the Political Bureau and head of the Arab and Islamic Relations Office of the Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas, who has traveled to Tehran for consultations with Iranian officials, met with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday afternoon. During the meeting, Naim conveyed warm greetings from Khalil al-Hayya, the newly appointed head of Hamas’ Political Bureau, to Araghchi. He also reiterated the condolences of Hamas leaders and the Palestinian people over the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Imam Khamenei, as well as a number of Iranian commanders, figures and citizens. He paid tribute to Iran’s martyred leader for his role in defending the sacred cause of the liberation of Palestine and Al-Quds. The Hamas Political Bureau member also briefed Araghchi on the latest developments in Palestine, including the continued “brutal crimes” by the Israeli regime in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, the Judaization of Al-Quds, and the brutal torture of Palestinians in prisons run by the occupying regime. Naim said the approach of the Israeli regime’s “criminal prime minister” was to continue fomenting war, committing genocide against Palestinians and forcibly displacing the Palestinian people by maintaining the inhumane policy of imposing a blockade and preventing humanitarian aid from entering the Gaza Strip. He called for serious and immediate action by the international community, particularly Islamic countries, to confront Israeli aggression and crimes against the Palestinian people and support the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination. Araghchi, for his part, thanked Hamas leadership for sending messages of condolence and sympathy and expressing solidarity with the Islamic Republic and the Iranian people. He stressed Iran’s principled and firm position on continuing comprehensive defense of the country against aggressors, as well as supporting the sacred cause of the liberation of Palestine and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with Al-Quds as its capital. The Iranian foreign minister also stressed that the Islamic Republic would continue its efforts to support the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people in international forums, including meetings of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and BRICS, as well as the upcoming session of the United Nations General Assembly.

item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://en.mfa.gov.ir/portal/newsview/793683

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs strongly condemns the aggressive actions taken by the United States against our beloved homeland on Tuesday night, September 1, and reaffirms the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to firmly defend Iran’s independence, national sovereignty, and territorial integrity. The US regime, having been driven to desperation in the face of the Iranian people’s ironclad resolve to defend the country, once again violated Iran’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity on Tuesday night, September 1, 2026, by attacking several civilian areas and service infrastructure, including a number of telecommunications towers and sites in the provinces of Khuzestan, Sistan and Baluchestan, Hormozgan, and Kerman. As a result, a number of our compatriots were martyred or wounded, and damage was inflicted on public and private property. In the attack by the American enemy on a wedding celebration in Kuhestak, located in Sirik County, Hormozgan Province, more than 70 of our compatriots were martyred or wounded, most of them women and children. These brutal war crimes, which constitute a flagrant violation of the fundamental principles of international law, are reminiscent of previous American-Zionist crimes over the past year and a half, including those in Minab and Lamerd. In response to the US military aggression, the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran, pursuant to their inherent right of self-defense, launched defensive and devastating strikes against US military bases that had served as the launching points for and provided support to the US military aggression against Iran. The Islamic Republic of Iran strongly calls on the countries of the region to prevent the continuation and expansion of the flames of war in the region by denying the American aggressors the use of their facilities and territory to prepare for and carry out acts of aggression against Iran, and not to allow the sinister US-Zionist plot to impose permanent insecurity on the region to be realized. While expressing its condolences over the martyrdom of our dear compatriots, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs reminds all governments of their responsibility to pursue, prosecute, and punish the perpetrators and those who ordered grave violations of international humanitarian law. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs once again reminds the United Nations, particularly the Security Council and the UN Secretary-General, of their responsibility to fulfill their duties in accordance with the UN Charter. The silence and inaction of the organs of the United Nations in the face of the continued violation of the fundamental principles and rules of the Charter, particularly Article 2(4), by a permanent member of the Security Council will further undermine the credibility of the Organization and pose an increasing threat to international peace and security.
